source.filename: receipt_mcdonalds_cck.jpg (the user's receipt photo, as the web app re-encodes it before upload)
source.note: the browser (Chromium) shrinks and re-encodes a photo before posting it, so its bytes, and this key, differ from the original file's (a8fa37448029); the same answer is recorded under both keys
source.ocr_text: the text app/extract/ocr.py::extract_text returned for exactly these posted bytes on the box, 2026-09-27; the offsets below index into it

fields.gst_reg_no: read from the photo: 'M2-0023981-4'; the OCR garbles it ('¥2-0029981-4'), so the offsets point at the garbled token
fields.invoice_no: read from the photo: 300882600036782 (this OCR misreads one digit, '300862600036782', so the offsets point at that token)
fields.issued_on: read from the photo: 10/04/2025, day first (Singapore), so 10 April 2025
fields.subtotal: DERIVED, not printed: the receipt prints one subtotal that already includes GST (15.00), so the net amount is total minus GST, 13.76 (13.76 x 9% = 1.24), which is what lets the arithmetic check pass; it has no offsets
fields.tax: read from the photo: 'TOTAL INCLUDES GST OF 1.24' (this OCR reads '4.24', so the offsets point at that token)
